title: Stele of Shemai
culture: Egypt, Aswan, Qubbet el-Hawa, excavations of Lady William Cecil, 1904, "Cecil Tombs," no. 28, Middle Kingdom (2040–1648 BCE), Dynasty 12, probably reign of Senusret I (1971–1926 BCE)
text_changes: None; translated fields and remarks reproduced verbatim

passages.text:
The one honored before Osiris, lord of Busiris,
the great god, lord of Anydos, that he may give invocation-offerings of bread and beer, oxen and fowl,
linen and travertine (vessels) to the ka of the chief of police, Shermai, vindicated.

An offering that the king gives to Anubis, he who is on his mountain, he who is in the place of embalming, lord of the cemetery, that he (Anubis) may give a thosand of bread and beer, oxen and gowl, linen adn travertine (vessels), of [ferings, and provisions?...]
passages.remark: Beginning in the center and continuing down the jamb on the right.

passages.text: An offering that the king gives to Osiris, lord of Busiris, the great god, lord of abydos [that he (Osiris) may give...]
passages.remark: Beginning in the center and continuing down the jamb on the left.

description: Two techniques of relief carving are employed here: the scene of the deceased seated before a table of offerings and its accompanying inscriptions are in raised relief, while the border inscriptions are in sunk relief. The three columns of hieroglyphs in the center read: "The one honored before Osiris, lord of Busiris, the great god, lord of Abydos, that he [the god] may give invocation-offerings of bread and beer, oxen and fowl, travertine [vases] and clothing to the ka [vital spirit] of the chief of police, Shemai, vindicated."
